items.title: Why does specificity keep climbing in one codebase but not another?
items.description: L2's own claim: selectors written by following DOM ancestor structure (like `#app .toolbar .btn`) pick up roughly one extra class per nesting level, so specificity grows with how deep the markup nests. A flat, class-per-component convention (utility-first or BEM) stays at exactly one class no matter how deep the DOM gets. Drag the nesting depth to see the two curves diverge.
